version_metadata.title: Primes in arithmetic progressions to large moduli I: Fixed residue classes

fixed_target_a_exact_source.source_text:
We will view
a
(the residue class we count arithmetic functions in to different moduli
q
) as a fixed positive integer throughout the paper, and any constants implied by asymptotic notation will be allowed to depend on
a
from this point onwards. Similarly, throughout the paper, we will let
\epsilon
be a single fixed small real number;
\epsilon=10^{-100}
would probably suffice. Any bounds in our asymptotic notation will also be allowed to depend on
\epsilon
.

SW_complete_definition.source_text:
Definition 1
(Siegel-Walfisz condition)
.
We say that a complex sequence
\alpha_{n}
satisfies the
Siegel-Walfisz condition
if for every
d\geq 1
,
q\geq 1
and
(a,q)=1
and every
A>1
we have
(6.1)
\Bigl|\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\sim N\\
n\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)\\
(n,d)=1\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n}-\frac{1}{\phi(q)}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\sim N\\
(n,dq)=1\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n}\Bigr|\ll_{A}\frac{N\tau(d)^{B_{0}}}{(\log{N})^{A}}.

scope_and_notation.interpretation: The paper explicitly fixes the target residue a as a positive integer throughout and permits all asymptotic constants to depend on a. It does not assert uniformity for a family with a moving up to X^(1+kappa), nor a uniform signed-target extension. Its SW definition must not be confused with such a target-residue-uniform final estimate.

Proposition_14_4.literal_source:
Proposition 14.4
(Reduction to exponential sums)
.
Let
\alpha_{n},\beta_{m},\gamma_{q,d},\lambda_{q,d,r}
be complex sequences with
|\alpha_{n}|,|\beta_{n}|\leq\tau(n)^{B_{0}}
and
|\gamma_{q,d}|\leq\tau(qd)^{B_{0}}
and
|\lambda_{q,d,r}|\leq\tau(qdr)^{B_{0}}
. Let
\alpha_{n}
and
\lambda_{q,d,r}
be supported on integers with
P^{-}(n)\geq z_{0}
and
P^{-}(r)\geq z_{0}
, and let
\alpha_{n}
satisfy the Siegel-Walfisz condition (
6.1
). Let
\mathscr{S}:=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d\sim D\\
(d,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}q\sim Q\\
(q,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}r\sim R\\
(r,a)=1\end{subarray}}\lambda_{q,d,r}\gamma_{q,d}\sum_{m\sim M}\beta_{m}\sum_{n\sim N}\alpha_{n}\Bigl(\mathbf{1}_{mn\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qrd)}-\frac{\mathbf{1}_{(mn,qrd)=1}}{\phi(qrd)}\Bigr).
Let
A>0
,
1\leq E\leq x
and
C=C(A,B_{0})
be sufficiently large in terms of
A,B_{0}
, and let
N,M
satisfy
N>QDE(\log{x})^{C},\qquad M>(\log{x})^{C}.
Then we have
|\mathscr{S}|\ll_{A,B_{0}}\frac{x}{(\log{x})^{A}}+MD^{1/2}Q^{1/2}(\log{x})^{O_{B_{0}}(1)}\Bigl(|\mathscr{E}_{1}|^{1/2}+|\mathscr{E}_{2}|^{1/2}\Bigr),
where
\displaystyle\mathscr{E}_{1}
\displaystyle:=\sum_{e\sim E}\mu^{2}(e)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}q\\
(q,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d\sim D\\
(d,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}r_{1},r_{2}\sim R\\
(r_{1}r_{2},a)=1\end{subarray}}\psi_{0}\Bigl(\frac{q}{Q}\Bigr)\frac{\lambda_{q,d,r_{1}}\overline{\lambda_{q,d,r_{2}}}}{\phi(qder_{2})qdr_{1}}
\displaystyle\qquad\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n_{1},n_{2}\sim N\\
(n_{1},qder_{1})=1\\
(n_{2},qder_{2})=1\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n_{1}}\overline{\alpha_{n_{2}}}\sum_{1\leq|h|\leq H_{1}}\widehat{\psi}_{0}\Bigl(\frac{hM}{qdr_{1}}\Bigr)e\Bigl(\frac{ah\overline{n_{1}}}{qdr_{1}}\Bigr),
\displaystyle\mathscr{E}_{2}
\displaystyle:=\sum_{e\sim E}\mu^{2}(e)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}q\\
(q,a)=1\end{subarray}}\psi_{0}\Bigl(\frac{q}{Q}\Bigr)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d\sim D\\
(d,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}r_{1},r_{2}\sim R\\
(r_{1},ar_{2})=1\\
(r_{2},aqdr_{1})=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\lambda_{q,d,r_{1}}\overline{\lambda_{q,d,r_{2}}}}{qdr_{1}r_{2}}
\displaystyle\qquad\times\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n_{1},n_{2}\sim N\\
n_{1}\equiv n_{2}\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qde)\\
(n_{1},n_{2}eqdr_{1})=1\\
(n_{2},n_{1}eqdr_{2})=1\\
|n_{1}-n_{2}|\geq N/(\log{x})^{C}\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n_{1}}\overline{\alpha_{n_{2}}}\sum_{1\leq|h|\leq H_{2}}\widehat{\psi}_{0}\Bigl(\frac{hM}{qdr_{1}r_{2}}\Bigr)e\Bigl(\frac{ah\overline{n_{1}r_{2}}}{qdr_{1}}+\frac{ah\overline{n_{2}qdr_{1}}}{r_{2}}\Bigr),
\displaystyle H_{1}
\displaystyle:=\frac{QDR}{M}\log^{5}{x},
\displaystyle H_{2}
\displaystyle:=\frac{QDR^{2}}{M}\log^{5}{x}.
Remark
.
To avoid confusion, we emphasize to the reader that in the above proposition (and elsewhere in the paper),
e
is the integer in the outer summation, except for when we use the function
e(x)=e^{2\pi ix}
. The distinction between the two should be clear from the context, and in most situations when this is used the variable
e
will just be the constant 1.
required_local_hypotheses_paraphrase: Complex alpha_n,beta_m,gamma_(q,d),lambda_(q,d,r), bounded by tau(n)^B0/tau(qd)^B0/tau(qdr)^B0 as displayed.
alpha is supported on Pminus(n)>=z0 and lambda on Pminus(r)>=z0; alpha satisfies SW(6.1).
S has (d,a)=(q,a)=(r,a)=1 and the original centered primitive mean modulo qrd.
A>0; 1<=E<=x; sufficiently large C=C(A,B0); N>QDE(logx)^C and M>(logx)^C.
Conclusion is a reduction with explicit E1/E2, not a complete bound for those exponential sums. H1=QDR/M log^5x, H2=QDR²/M log^5x.
Global convention fixes positive a and allows constants/thresholds to depend on it.
Proposition_14_4.source_visible_scale_qualification: The local displayed Prop14.4 statement does not itself print NM asymp x or all upper scale caps; its proof and applications use the convolution scale, while Lemma14.5 explicitly prints NM asymp x. This audit does not silently manufacture a corrected standalone quantifier theorem. The actual intended caller x~UV does supply that scale relation.

Lemma_14_5_not_Proposition.literal_source:
Lemma 14.5
(Simplification of exponential sum)
.
Let
N,M,Q,R\leq x
with
NM\asymp x
and
(14.9)
\displaystyle QR
\displaystyle<x^{2/3},
(14.10)
\displaystyle QR^{2}
\displaystyle<Mx^{1-2\epsilon}.
Let
\lambda_{q,r}
and
\alpha_{n}
be complex sequences supported on
P^{-}(n),P^{-}(r)\geq z_{0}
with
|\lambda_{q,r}|\leq\tau(qr)^{B_{0}}
and
|\alpha_{n}|\leq\tau(n)^{B_{0}}
. Let
H:=\frac{QR^{2}}{M}\log^{5}{x}
and let
\displaystyle\mathscr{E}
\displaystyle:=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}(q,a)=1\end{subarray}}\psi_{0}\Bigl(\frac{q}{Q}\Bigr)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}r_{1},r_{2}\sim R\\
(r_{1},ar_{2})=1\\
(r_{2},aqr_{2})=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\lambda_{q,r_{1}}\overline{\lambda_{q,r_{2}}}}{qr_{1}r_{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n_{1},n_{2}\sim N\\
n_{1}\equiv n_{2}\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)\\
(n_{1},n_{2}qr_{1})=1\\
(n_{2},n_{1}qr_{2})=1\\
|n_{1}-n_{2}|\geq N/(\log{x})^{C}\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n_{1}}\overline{\alpha_{n_{2}}}
\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\times\sum_{1\leq|h|\leq H}\widehat{\psi}_{0}\Bigl(\frac{hM}{qr_{1}r_{2}}\Bigr)e\Bigl(\frac{ah\overline{n_{1}r_{2}}}{qr_{1}}+\frac{ah\overline{n_{2}qr_{1}}}{r_{2}}\Bigr).
Then we have (uniformly in
C
)
\mathscr{E}\ll_{B_{0}}\exp((\log\log{x})^{5})\sup_{\begin{subarray}{c}H^{\prime}\leq H\\
Q^{\prime}\leq 2Q\\
R_{1},R_{2}\leq 2R\end{subarray}}|\mathscr{E}^{\prime}|+\frac{N^{2}}{Qx^{\epsilon}},
where
\mathscr{E}^{\prime}=\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}Q\leq q\leq Q^{\prime}\\
(q,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}R\leq r_{1}\leq R_{1}\\
R\leq r_{2}\leq R_{2}\\
(r_{1}ar_{2})=1\\
(r_{2},aqr_{1})=1\end{subarray}}\frac{\lambda_{q,r_{1}}\overline{\lambda_{q,r_{2}}}}{qr_{1}r_{2}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n_{1},n_{2}\sim N\\
n_{1}\equiv n_{2}\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)\\
(n_{1},qr_{1}n_{2})=1\\
(n_{2},qr_{2}n_{1})=1\\
(n_{1}r_{2},n_{2})\in\mathcal{N}\\
|n_{1}-n_{2}|\geq N/(\log{x})^{C}\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n_{1}}\overline{\alpha_{n_{2}}}\sum_{1\leq|h|\leq H^{\prime}}e\Bigl(\frac{ah\overline{n_{2}qr_{1}}(n_{1}-n_{2})}{n_{1}r_{2}}\Bigr),
and
\mathcal{N}
is a set with the property that if
(a,b)\in\mathcal{N}
and
(a^{\prime},b^{\prime})\in\mathcal{N}
then we have
\gcd(a,b^{\prime})=\gcd(a^{\prime},b)=1
.
required_hypotheses_paraphrase: Complex lambda_(q,r),alpha_n with rough supports Pminus(n),Pminus(r)>=z0 and divisor-power bounds.
E is the specifically displayed coprime/off-diagonal shared-q exponential sum with H=QR²/M log^5x and n1 congruent n2 mod q.
The output removes Fourier weight and passes to a cross-coprime partition, paying exp((loglogx)^5), plus N²/(Q*x^epsilon); the paper says uniform in C, not in the globally fixed target a.

finite_shared_qd_Cauchy_step.exact_Cauchy_passage:
We now apply Cauchy-Schwarz in the
e
,
b
,
m
,
q
and
d
variables, which allows us to eliminate the
\beta_{m}
and
\gamma_{q,d}
coefficients. This gives
\displaystyle|\mathscr{S}|^{2}
\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{\mathscr{E}_{0}^{2}}\Bigl(\sum_{e\sim E}\sum_{q\sim Q}\sum_{d\sim D}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}m\sim M\\
(m,qd)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}b\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qde)\\
b\equiv a\overline{m}\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qd)\end{subarray}}|\gamma_{q,d}|^{2}|\beta_{m}|^{2}\Bigr)\mathscr{S}^{\prime}+O_{A}\Bigl(\frac{x^{2}}{(\log{x})^{2A}}\Bigr)
\displaystyle\ll MQD(\log{x})^{O_{B_{0}}(1)}\mathscr{S}^{\prime}+O_{A}\Bigl(\frac{x^{2}}{(\log{x})^{2A}}\Bigr),
where
\displaystyle\mathscr{S}^{\prime}
\displaystyle:=\sum_{e\sim E}\mu^{2}(e)\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}q\sim Q\\
(q,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}d\sim D\\
(d,a)=1\end{subarray}}\sum_{m\sim M}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}b\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qde)\\
b\equiv a\overline{m}\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qd)\\
(b,qde)=1\end{subarray}}
\displaystyle\qquad\times\Bigl|\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}r\sim R\\
(r,ae)=1\end{subarray}}\lambda_{q,d,r}\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}n\sim N\\
(n,e)=1\end{subarray}}\alpha_{n}\Bigl(\mathbf{1}_{\begin{subarray}{c}mn\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qdr)\\
n\equiv b\ (\mathrm{mod}\ qde)\end{subarray}}-\frac{\mathbf{1}_{(mn,qdr)=1}}{\phi(qdre)}\Bigr)\Bigr|^{2}.
finite_shared_qd_Cauchy_step.what_is_finite: After the exact/current admissible residue grouping, Cauchy is in the SAME e,b,m,q,d indices. Thus both r1/r2 copies retain shared q,d, and opening the square retains n1 congruent n2 mod qde. Complex conjugate lambda/alpha weights are explicit. This structural finite step does not need a small or fixed target residue if directly reproved with its actual coprimality hypotheses.
finite_shared_qd_Cauchy_step.not_all_of_Prop144_is_finite: The preceding rough-support deletions and the subsequent estimates for S1,S2,S3 are analytic estimates using divisor means, Poisson tails and SW. They cannot be imported merely from the Cauchy identity.
finite_shared_qd_Cauchy_step.mapping_to_actual_route: For original smoothing M=V and paired alpha length N=U, shared qd is the original shared q1 (or an explicitly defined further factorization thereof). The remaining factor r corresponds to the remaining physical factors. A dictionary must retain all original complex labels and the original primitive center; this audit does not supply a completed Lean theorem.

pure_CRT_reciprocity.finding: Bezout/CRT identities are exact arithmetic identities for the numerator; no size bound on a is needed.

Poisson_tail.finding: The full Poisson formula retains e(ha/q), and its absolute tail proof uses this phase norm1. No small-a derivative bound is used in that lemma: the cutoff and Fourier decay depend on f,M,q, not on the chosen residue representative. The printed scale caps M,q<=x and tail hypotheses still must be checked.

divisor_shift_gate.complete_source:
Lemma 8.7
(Divisor function bounds)
.
Let
|b|<x-y
and
y\geq qx^{\epsilon}
. Then we have
\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}x-y\leq n\leq x\\
n\equiv a\ (\mathrm{mod}\ q)\end{subarray}}\tau(n)^{C}\tau(n-b)^{C}\ll\frac{y}{q}(\tau(q)\log{x})^{O_{C}(1)}.
Proof.
This follows from Shiu’s Theorem
[
33
]
, and is given in
[
4
, Lemma 12]
.
divisor_shift_gate.finding: Lemma8.7 explicitly assumes |b|<x-y and y>=q*x^epsilon. Uses in14.2/14.3 involving tau(mn-a) are protected by fixed a for sufficiently large convolution scale; they are not a uniform moving-shift estimate as printed. Exact mn=a is eventually absent in the fixed-a positive dyadic setting, but may occur for moving a~UV. Actual cleaned-alpha support n not dividing a can remove exact products, which is necessary but does not itself prove every required shifted divisor mean.

decisive_slow_phase_deletion.exact_source:

Since
|h|\leq H=(QR\log^{5}{x})/M

The error term above contributes to

Therefore if (

decisive_slow_phase_deletion.finding: With the statement H=QR²/M log^5x, the slow fraction size is O(|a| log^5x/(MN))=O(|a| log^5x/x). The displayed O(log^6x/x) suppresses a as allowed by the fixed-a convention. Faithfully tracking the proof gives an |a| multiplier on the two total-error monomials, not a residue-uniform N²/(Q*x^epsilon) for moving |a|~x or larger.
decisive_slow_phase_deletion.faithful_total_error_scale: Up to coefficient/log losses, |a|*(N²/Q)*(QR²/(M*x)+Q²R²/x²). Fixed a can be swallowed; the displayed geometry alone does not cancel |a|.

slow_weight_derivatives_if_retained.finding: Keeping the slow factor avoids the incorrect moving-residue deletion. Its normalized phase/variation scale is of size |a|H/(QR²N)~|a|/x*log^5x. With actual |a|<=X^(1+kappa) this is a genuine X^kappa-type cost, not a uniformly O(1/x) perturbation. A valid derivative/partial-summation lemma on the actual carrier and honest geometric payment is required.
slow_weight_derivatives_if_retained.caller_gate_retained: 0<=kappa<=sigma/100 permits 5*kappa<=sigma/20, so a degree-five variation loss may be payable; no impossibility claim for the new retained-slow-phase route is made.

later_frequency_size.finding: Lemma15.2 defines ell=a*(...), but its displayed dyadic numerator cap L<<R²N³ log²x/M suppresses the same fixed a. Even after repairing14.5, a moving-residue extension of this downstream spectral stage must track the changed numerator range/energy, not cite the fixed-a theorem unchanged.

a_dependence_audit.uniformity_conclusion: Paper I supplies fixed-positive-residue reductions and estimates under its convention. It does not supply the actual signed moving-residue analytic endpoint. Fixed a implies a<=x^eta eventually for any fixed eta>0 with an a-dependent threshold; the actual lower gate |a|>=c0X prevents using that implication uniformly.

literal_source_anomalies_and_required_di.literal: Statement H=QR²/M log^5x, proof sentence prints H=QR/M log^5x. HTML alttext confirms the discrepancy. This audit uses the larger statement H when evaluating the slow fraction, not a silent advantageous correction.

Several displayed conditions contain (r2,a*q*r2)=1 or (r1*a*r2)=1 instead of the consistent distinct-factor coprimalities appearing nearby. HTML alttext confirms these source strings. They must be reconciled in any exact formal dictionary, not silently used as an analytic theorem.

Global n~N is N<n<=2N, while the E-sum uses e~E and 1<=E. Taken literally E=1 has e=2; the remark says e will often just be constant1. This is a specialization/convention issue, not an obstruction to reproving the finite singleton-e=1 Cauchy route. Taking E=1/2 would leave the printed 1<=E premise and so also needs an adapted proof rather than literal invocation.
